title: Catch-Up Amount for a Late Rent Month — Apartment Home Lease Ledger
content:
The catch-up amount of an Apartment Home Lease is worked out on the most recent late billing period — the billing period of the latest initial late fee line — from that period's lines on the lease ledger.

## Definitions

**(1) The period's rent** is its base rent line less the rent concession, preferred employer discount and military discount credits posted for the period, never below zero.

**(2) The period's recurring fees** are its lease fee lines.

**(3) The period's late fees** are its late fee lines less the courtesy waiver and charge reversal credits posted for the period, never below zero.

**(4) The period's payments** are the lease payments received during the month ending on the handling date (dated after the same day number of the previous month), less the returned payments dated in that month, never below zero.

**(5) Application.** The period's payments are applied in the charter order: to its recurring fees first and its late fees next, and to its rent last. In a community whose state puts rent first (Colorado), they go to its rent first, then to its recurring fees, then to its late fees. Each part takes no more than its own amount before the rest passes on.

**(6) The catch-up amount** is the period's rent still unpaid after that application, plus all of its recurring fees still unpaid, plus all of its late fees still unpaid, plus the monthly rent in force when the handling date falls on one of the 10 days before the next rent due date (the day after the period's last day), rounded half up to the cent.

## The next-month window

The next rent due date is the day after the last day of the late period. "One of the 10 days before" means the handling date is between 1 and 10 days before that date.

| Late period | Next rent due date | Handling dates that add the monthly rent |
|---|---|---|
| April (30 days) | 1 May | 21 April through 30 April |
| February 2026 (28 days) | 1 March 2026 | 19 February through 28 February 2026 |

A handling date of 20 April, or of 1 May itself, adds nothing for an April period.

## Worked example (hypothetical ledger, community outside Colorado)

Period lines: base rent line $1,800.00, no rent credits; recurring fees $94.00; late fee lines $130.00, no waiver or reversal. Payments received in the month ending on the handling date: $1,000.00.

1. Applied to recurring fees: $94.00, leaving $906.00.
2. Applied to late fees: $130.00, leaving $776.00.
3. Applied to rent: $776.00; rent still unpaid $1,024.00; recurring fees and late fees still unpaid $0.00.
4. Handling date 12 April: outside the 10 days before 1 May, so the catch-up amount is **$1,024.00**.
5. Handling date 25 April: inside the window, so the monthly rent of $1,800.00 is added and the catch-up amount is **$2,824.00**.

The same ledger in a Colorado community applies the $1,000.00 to rent first: rent still unpaid $800.00, recurring fees $94.00 and late fees $130.00 still unpaid, a catch-up amount of $1,024.00 on 12 April.
